bullets.title: What’s in My Bag, 2023
bullets.note: I have never met anyone more meticulous about everyday carry than [Matt Mullenweg](https://tim.blog/2022/03/09/matt-mullenweg-antarctica/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf). Each year, he publishes an updated “What’s in my bag” blog post, and [this is the latest](https://ma.tt/2023/12/the-bag-post/). For a fun comparison, [see this photo](https://ma.tt/2014/08/whats-in-my-bag/) of Matt’s gadgets from nearly a decade ago.

bullets.title: Masterpieces of Fantasy Art
bullets.creator: Dian Hanson
bullets.note: . This is a sumptuous dive back into the most gorgeous art I met through _Heavy Metal_ magazine, fantasy nerdom, and everything in between. I think of it as a buffet of creative inspiration, as the styles vary widely. From the official description: “Fantasy art, that colorful blend of myth, muscle and sexy maidens, took off in 1923 with the launch of _Weird Tales_ magazine, was reinvigorated in the 1960s with _The Lord of the Rings_, _Conan the Barbarian_ paperbacks with Frank Frazetta covers, and the late ’60s emergence of fantasy psychedelia. This book features original paintings, contextualized by preparatory sketches, sculptures, calendars, magazines, and paperback books, for an immersive dive into this dynamic, fanciful genre.”

bullets.section: Slightly healthier junk food I’ll weave into the holidays
bullets.title: Tate’s Bake Shop Ginger Zinger Cookies
bullets.note: I can easily finish an entire bag of these chewy beauties on cheat day. They are gluten-free, which I only learned after the fact. Tate’s [Chocolate Chip Cookies](https://www.amazon.com/Tates-Bake-Shop-Chocolate-Cookies/dp/B00B62W306?th=1) are also fantastic, but the Ginger Zingers are my hands-down fave. In between butter cookies and gingerbread men, I’ll have a few of these around Christmas to convince myself I’m behaving.
